record.paper_title: Open Problems on Graph Coloring for Special Graph Classes
record.original_question: For a connected graph, the diameter is the maximum distance between two vertices, where distance is the length of a shortest path. The 3-Coloring problem asks whether a graph has a proper coloring using colors {1, 2, 3}. The List 3-Coloring problem asks whether a graph with lists L(v) contained in {1, 2, 3} for each vertex v has a proper coloring that assigns every vertex a color from its list. What is the computational complexity of 3-Coloring for graphs of diameter 2, and what is the computational complexity of List 3-Coloring for graphs of diameter 2?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 6 Determine the complexity of the problems 3-Coloring and List 3-Coloring for graphs of diameter 2.
The diameter of G is the maximum of maxv d(u, v) over all vertices u in G.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G = (V, E)$ be a finite, simple, connected, undirected graph. The distance $d(u,v)$ between two vertices $u, v \in V$ is the length (number of edges) of a shortest path from $u$ to $v$, and the diameter of $G$ is $\max_{u,v \in V} d(u,v)$. A proper $3$-coloring of $G$ is a map $c : V 	o \{1,2,3\}$ such that $c(u) 
eq c(v)$ whenever $uv \in E$. In the 3-Coloring problem, given $G$, one must decide whether $G$ admits a proper $3$-coloring. In the List 3-Coloring problem, each vertex $v \in V$ is additionally equipped with a list $L(v) \subseteq \{1,2,3\}$, and one must decide whether $G$ admits a proper $3$-coloring $c$ with $c(v) \in L(v)$ for all $v \in V$.

Determine the computational complexity of the 3-Coloring problem and of the List 3-Coloring problem when the input graph $G$ is restricted to have diameter at most $2$. In particular, are these problems solvable in polynomial time, or are they NP-complete, on the class of graphs of diameter $2$?
artifact.status_search_result: The complexity of 3-Coloring (and List 3-Coloring) restricted to diameter-2 graphs remains a well-known open problem. No polynomial-time algorithm or NP-hardness proof is known. The best known algorithms are subexponential: Mertzios and Spirakis (2012/2016) achieved $2^{O(\sqrt{n \log n})}$, and Dębski, Piecyk, and Rzążewski (ESA 2021 / SIDMA) improved this to $2^{O(n^{1/3} \log^2 n)}$. NP-hardness is known for diameter-3 graphs but not for diameter-2 graphs.

status_evidence.title: Algorithms and Almost Tight Results for 3-Colorability of Small Diameter Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Subexponential algorithm 2^{O(sqrt{n log n})} for 3-coloring diameter-2 graphs; complexity status left open.
status_evidence.claim: 3-Coloring on diameter-2 graphs has a subexponential algorithm but its precise complexity is open.

status_evidence.title: Faster 3-Coloring of Small-Diameter Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithm solving 3-Coloring on n-vertex diameter-2 graphs in time 2^{O(n^{1/3} log^2 n)}; complexity remains open.
status_evidence.claim: Improved subexponential algorithm exists, but P vs NP-hard status for diameter-2 3-Coloring is still open.
